title: Deleting a completed audit's "cannot delete a completed audit" guard is bypassed automatically and silently — the frontend sets `force=true` itself whenever the audit is completed, with no reason, no elevated permission, and the same generic confirm dialog as any other delete
description:
**Checklist row:** §4.5 — Justification required on destructive/terminal actions: closing, revoking, or rejecting a record requires a mandatory note/reason, not a bare status flip.
**Files:** `intelligent-audit.controller.js:897-917` (`deleteIntelligentAudit`) does soft-delete correctly (`audit.status = 'archived'`, not a physical delete) and correctly blocks deleting a `completed` audit — `if (audit.status === 'completed' && !req.query.force) throw AppError.badRequest(...)` — but the override requires only the same `audit.delete` permission as any other delete, no additional reason/justification field, and no elevated permission (e.g. an `audit.admin`-style override). Worse, `PreAuditsTable.jsx:99` (`handleDeleteConfirm`) computes `const force = auditToDelete.status === 'completed';` and passes it automatically — the guard is bypassed by the standard delete button itself, with zero extra confirmation step, warning copy, or reason capture in the shared `AlertDialog` (lines 486-520), which is the same generic 'Are you sure?' dialog used for deleting a draft/in-progress audit.
**Root Cause:** The `force=true` escape hatch was intended as a deliberate, presumably rare admin override, but the frontend wires it as the default, automatic behavior for the one case (a completed audit) the backend guard exists specifically to protect — so in practice the guard never actually stops anyone using the real UI.
**Impact:** A completed intelligent audit — the module's own terminal, presumably-finalized record, potentially already handed off to `audit-assurance` via `AuditAssuranceService.importFromIntelliAudit` — can be archived by any `audit.delete` holder with a single click and the exact same low-friction confirmation as deleting a half-finished draft. No rationale is captured anywhere (not in the request, not in `_logAuditEvent`'s `meta: { auditName }`, which records only the audit's name), so an auditor asking 'who decided to retire this completed audit, and why' finds nothing beyond actor and timestamp.
**Claude Fix Prompt:**
In `intelligent-audit.controller.js`'s `deleteIntelligentAudit`, require and persist a reason when `force` is used: `if (audit.status === 'completed') { if (!req.query.force) throw AppError.badRequest('Cannot delete a completed audit. Use ?force=true with a reason to override.'); const { reason } = req.body; if (!reason || reason.trim().length < 25) throw AppError.badRequest('A reason of at least 25 characters is required to delete a completed audit'); }` — then include `reason` in the `_logAuditEvent` call's `meta`. In `PreAuditsTable.jsx`, when `auditToDelete.status === 'completed'`, render a distinct, more serious confirmation (different copy, a required `Textarea` for the reason, passed through to `preAuditService.deleteIntelligentAudit(id, force, reason)`) instead of silently reusing the generic draft-delete dialog.
